newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air Liquide in Japanese deal.
newsitem.headline: Air Liquide in Japanese deal.

text.p: French industrial gas company Air Liquide said on Monday its Japanese unit Teisan had signed a long-term deal to supply oxygen and nitrogen to a major Japanese chemical firm.

Air Liquide said in a statement that under the agreement, Teisan would supply via pipeline 250 tons per day of oxygen and nitrogen to the Omi plant belonging to Denki Kagaku Kogyo KK. It gave no value for the deal.
The Omi plant, located in Japan's Niigata prefecture, is the world's largest carbide chemical plant, Air Liquide said.

Up to now, Denki Kagaku Kogyo met its own requirements for oxygen and nitrogen using plants made by Teisan but it now had decided to let Teisan handle all gas-related activities such as gas production and plant maintenance, Air Liquide said.
Air Liquide group said it would also invest in a new Japanese plant to be started by the end of 1997 that would employ the most advanced technologies in cyrogenic air separation.
